verdicts.reason: Quote states forwarding of PSLVERR with PREADY; checkable every cycle from interface signals (o_apb_pslverr vs o_apb_pready). Actor is the bridge, not interconnect; the bridge sits on the requester-facing side as completer, so slave.
Quote says next transfer is independent; this is a bridge property, actor should be the bridge (slave side), not interconnect. Scenario check is fine (error transfer followed by a normal one).
Bridge waiting indefinitely with PREADY low is bridge behavior; actor should be bridge (slave), not interconnect. Scenario is appropriate since unbounded wait is not assertion-checkable.
Recovery is by a system watchdog or reset (integration-level); 'Cleared by reset' is descriptive of recovery options, not a hard bridge requirement. Keep scenario; strength downgraded to SHOULD.
Quote: reset clears all state and the in-flight transfer is lost; the bridge does this, not the interconnect. Scenario check is fine.
Bridge uses Setup-cycle values and ignores PENABLE without Setup; actor is the bridge (slave). The 'not detected' part is non-verifiable, but the ignore behavior can be exercised.
Quote says behavior is unspecified and not detected; nothing to verify or exercise. It is a description of unspecified behavior.
No error output other than PSLVERR is checkable from interface signals (port list); actor is the bridge. Sticky error and counter are internal but absence of an output is checkable by interface.
Describes a lack of feature (no parity or ECC); nothing to verify or exercise, and corruption is not detected is not testable behavior.

duplicates.reason: Both rest on ERR-002 hang; but they differ in behavior (wait vs recovery) so not truly duplicates.

questions.question: AB2-12-01 and others use 'interconnect' as actor, but the quotes describe the bridge behavior. Which side (requester-facing or completer-facing) is the bridge treated as, and which actor label should be used?
For ERR-003, when a reset is asserted mid-transfer, are both resets required to be asserted together? Is the requester repeat part of the testbench model or a bridge requirement?
